claim: Hamblin (1970) broke the textbook 'standard treatment'; the standard definition (an argument that seems valid but is not) was then attacked by Massey's asymmetry thesis (no theory of invalidity), so a fallacy label cannot be settled by form alone.
agent_test: Compare an agent that labels by form-matching with one that must name the defect in the support; score on LOGIC items at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Modern theories treat fallacies as context-dependent: Walton ties them to dialogue type and illicit shifts between types; pragma-dialectics defines them as violations of 10 critical-discussion rules; Woods-Walton match fallacies to different logics. The same move can be sound in one dialogue type and a fallacy in another. No study found tests whether a dialogue-type tag lowers LLM false positives.
agent_test: Give the agent a dialogue-type tag (persuasion, inquiry, eristic) in the S1 marked block and measure false-positive rate on sound appeals to authority.

claim: Lay readers rate fallacious ad hominem fragments lower than sound ones, but only moderately (3.75 vs 5.29; replication 3.43 vs 5.27 on a 7-point scale); tu quoque is rated least bad, abusive worst.
agent_test: Use the human ratings as a prior for how much to discount a flagged argument; test calibration against human means.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Bayesian account: argument strength depends on prior belief, evidence polarity and source reliability, not on form. Reliability had by far the largest effect (5.58 vs 3.21, F(1,72)=198.63); polarity and prior effects were small but reproducible in Bayindir et al. 2005.
agent_test: Vary source reliability in a marked authority block and check that confidence shifts in the Bayesian direction at equal tokens. One research lineage (Oaksford and Hahn); Hahn and Oaksford 2007 itself was not opened (b25).

claim: Fine-tuned encoders detect fallacies far above chance on LOGIC (BERT 45.80, DeBERTa 50.29, Electra 53.31 micro-F1; structure-aware Electra 58.77), while zero-shot GPT-3 and MNLI models sit at the random level (12.0-13.7 vs random 12.02). Verified in the paper.
agent_test: Not an agent test; baseline for later detection tests. All figures come from Jin et al. 2022 (other papers reuse them).

claim: Fallacy detectors transfer poorly across datasets: on LOGIC Climate F1 falls to 22-27 (Jin), coarse 46-57 and fine about 24 (Sourati); CoCoLoFa-trained models lose 0.05 to 0.13 F1 on other sets and models trained elsewhere score 0.09-0.19 on it.
schema_part: S1 (do not trust a single detector)
agent_test: Run the agent's fallacy check on two datasets with different style and compare the drop at equal tokens.

claim: Benchmarks may measure scheme or source type rather than fallacy, and labels are noisy: a fine-tuned classifier flags 16.6% of CoCoLoFa's valid class but 58.9% of matched negatives; in MAFALDA 28% of 203 spans have 2+ valid labels and any single human annotator used as gold gives level-2 F1 only 0.09-0.14.
agent_test: Report agreement against several gold sets; do not tune a detector to one label set.

claim: Zero-shot LLMs are weak at fine-grained fallacy labelling: MAFALDA span F1 for GPT-3.5 is 0.627/0.201/0.138 (levels 0/1/2) vs human 0.749/0.352/0.186 (verified in the paper); GPT-4 reaches 48.38-49.78 macro-F1 on MAFALDA in a second study.
agent_test: Measure the agent's fine-label accuracy vs coarse (binary or level 0) at equal tokens; prefer coarse flags.

claim: Zero-shot GPT-4 can match fine-tuned T5 on some datasets (78.94 vs 83.20 on Argotario-style scores per paper table, 79.10 vs 80.42 on Reddit) but is far lower on harder ones (MAFALDA about 49; LOGIC 0.28 macro-F1 in Jeong et al.). Performance depends strongly on dataset.
agent_test: Same as K08; report per dataset, not one average.

claim: Multi-round prompting (warm-up, CoT, definitions) improves fallacy classification in 83.7% of experiments, average +1.27 to +7.54 macro-F1 by model; the warm-up round lowers the failure rate (12.27% vs 15.09% for zero-shot CoT). Few-shot helped only GPT-4.
agent_test: Compare a one-shot with a two-round fallacy check at equal total tokens. All numbers come from one group (Pan et al.); partly checked in the paper.

claim: Adding definitions or rules to fallacy prompts gives mixed, model-dependent results: rules hurt GPT-3.5 (0.30 to 0.12) but CoT helped GPT-4o (0.13 to 0.86) in one study; Prompt Ranking gains in Jeong et al. are large for gpt-3.5 (Covid 0.14 to 0.56) and small or negative for gpt-4 (Covid accuracy 0.93 to 0.86).
agent_test: Ablate definitions in the prompt per model at equal tokens; do not assume a prompt transfers.

claim: Explicit structure helps classification: a logical structure tree raises GPT-3.5 accuracy (Reddit 65.29 to 70.76, LOGIC 42.28 to 47.99) and Llama-2 on LOGIC 69.36 to 74.16; structure-aware Electra gains +5.46 F1.
agent_test: Test premise-conclusion extraction before labelling, at equal tokens.

claim: Training on fallacy data can help or hurt general reasoning: LFUD (fallacy-understanding data) gives +5% to +21% accuracy on LogiQA2.0, Reclor, TaxiNLI, FOLIO, but adding LOGIC data cut TaxiNLI from 68.54 to 40.60 (LLaMA2-13B). Training-based, outside our no-training scope.
agent_test: Not testable without training; note only.

claim: LLMs are convinced by fallacious arguments more often than by logical ones in debate: GPT-3.5 37% vs 29%, GPT-4 67% vs 37% of claims (200 claims x 3 runs); 41% and 69% relative increase. Numbers verified in the paper. Gap search: no independent replication found; LoFa (2026) is a related design, not a replication.
agent_test: Run a persuader with fallacious vs logical arguments against our agent at equal tokens and measure flip rate. One study (LOGICOM).

claim: Source cues bias judgement of fallacies: humans rate fallacious comments as more logically accurate when labelled human-written (3.35 vs 2.40 control, N=505); LLMs also follow invalid arguments, from 0.15% (best model) to 94.6% (GPT-4o) in a sycophancy benchmark, and are weak against fabricated authority cues.
schema_part: S1 (authority block marked, label stripped when judging)
agent_test: Strip source labels before judging an argument and compare the verdict with the labelled version.

claim: LLM robustness to fallacies rises with scale and differs by type: Llama-3.1 LFR@3 59.75 (8B), 70.38 (70B), 77.17 (405B); appeal to authority and equivocation are weakest; CoT helped most types (+7% to +13%) but hurt appeal to authority (-1.87%). Gap search: LoFa tested no 2026 model (API calls May-July 2025); GPT-4 authority LFR@3 39.20 (GPT-3.5 22.54); CoT changed authority by -1.87% in one GPT-4/NQ1 comparison (no benefit, not shown harmful).
agent_test: Test appeal to authority with a marked-block vs inline condition. One group; closed models via API only.

claim: Emotionally loaded rewording of fallacious arguments lowers HUMAN fallacy detection: crowd macro-F1 fell 14.5% on average (0.380-0.533 vs 0.563 original) and the share labelled fallacious dropped from 91% to 86%. CORRECTION (gap search): the earlier wording said LLM detection; it was human annotators. No study tests whether neutralising wording helps an LLM checker.
agent_test: Check LLM detection on original vs neutralised text at equal tokens (untested).

claim: Extra context or audio tone does not help LLM fallacy detection and theory-based taxonomy prompts do not beat a base prompt: accuracy text/context/context+audio 51/49/46 (base), 53/49/46 (pragma-dialectics), 44/45/25 (periodic table); base prompt recalled only 5% of Slippery Slope.
agent_test: Compare theory-based taxonomy prompts with a base prompt at equal tokens; expect no gain.

claim: Fallacies in real dialogue are rare and labelling them is reliable only with crowds: 0.2% of CMV posts are ad hominem (3,866 arguments) vs 19.5% of comments on news sites; crowd kappa 0.79; human upper bound accuracy 0.878. Verified in the paper.
agent_test: Set the flag threshold using base rates: most inputs should not be flagged.

claim: LLMs argue differently from humans and still produce fallacies: logical defence 67-76% and ethotic counterattack 15-17% vs humans 59% and 32%; Talk2AI found fallacies in 17% of user and 14.5% of LLM texts (3,080 conversations).
agent_test: Count fallacious moves in our agent's own output (self-audit at the end).

claim: LLM fallacy detectors give many unidentified outputs and false positives: 95 of 780 None predictions; accuracy 0.79 rises to 0.90 after removing them; nine models in Xu et al. all show high false-positive rates; adding a Prolog rule lifted several classes. Gap search: published false-positive rates are low mainly because the valid class holds few sound arguments that look like fallacies; scheme-matched sound arguments were flagged 58.9% (vs 16.6% native) by a fine-tuned encoder.
agent_test: Measure false-positive rate on sound arguments, not only recall.

claim: Fallacy-trap sets are hard for LLMs: RuozhiBench best model 62% vs humans above 90% (677 questions, 17 LLMs); DeflectBench refusal swings 80-100 points with frame or fallacy type.
agent_test: Test the agent on RuozhiBench-style trap questions at equal tokens.

claim: An LLM tutor for fallacies shows a small effect (LFTutor, N=20, p<0.05 and p<0.01, about 8.4% automatic gain).
agent_test: Small N; not usable.

claim: Using critical questions as a self-check gate on the model's own reasoning plan improves LLM-judge scores on MT-Bench reasoning and math by about 4.6% and 5.4% on average over plain/CoT prompting across 5 models, but about half the gain remains when the questions are removed and no token-matched comparison exists.
agent_test: Run the 8-question gate vs same-token self-consistency on a held-out reasoning set; report accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: A plain zero-shot LLM asked Walton-style critical questions is biased toward yes: GPT-4 answered yes to 53.3% of critical questions whose true answer was no, against 27.8% wrong for a fine-tuned RoBERTa.
agent_test: Force the check to state what would make each answer no; compare error rate on true-no questions.

claim: Fallacy detectors, fine-tuned and zero-shot, track the argumentation scheme rather than its misuse: sound arguments built on the same scheme as a fallacy (e.g. expert testimony that satisfies the expert-opinion critical questions) were flagged 58.9% (ModernBERT), 70.3% (RoBERTa) and 62.0% (Reddit-trained) vs 16.6%, 19.7%, 5.7% for the native valid class; Argotario authority 78.8% vs 11.7%.
schema_part: S1 (marked block must record competence checks, not just the presence of a citation)
agent_test: Score the S1 check on scheme-matched sound arguments (Scheme Foils) as well as fallacies; require the false-positive rate on them below a set bound.

claim: The false-positive rate of zero-shot LLM fallacy checks on sound scheme look-alikes depends on the prompt: native-to-matched gaps were +13.5 pp (Sonnet 5), +12.6 (Haiku 4.5), +0.5 (Qwen3.6-27B); a binary 'is it fallacious' prompt reversed the gap by -7.7, -33.2 and -25.6 pp, while naming a type kept the scheme-tracking effect (+31.0, +45.6, +25.5 pp).
agent_test: Ask the binary flawed/not-flawed question before any type naming; measure both rates.

claim: Resisting invalid pressure and accepting valid criticism are separable and trade off in 2026 models: compliance with invalid (fallacy, authority, consensus, emotion) arguments ranged 0.2% to 95% across ten models, while responsiveness to valid arguments ranged 32% to 95%; one model resisted (1%) but updated on only 32% of valid arguments.
agent_test: Test the agent with both argument types; reject designs that only cut compliance.

claim: Label ambiguity is large exactly where false positives are decided: two annotators agreed on 86.3% (kappa 0.74) of a 3-way coding but only 0.50 specific agreement on scheme-matched valid arguments; 12 of 237 CoCoLoFa comments written as fallacies were judged fallacy-like but valid. No paper compares model-human with human-human agreement on the same items.
agent_test: Keep an 'uncertain' label and report agreement with several gold sets.
